claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films and nanoribbons have high densities of interfaces, grain boundaries, structural disorder, and residual strain.

Interfacial and surface disorder, exchange-interaction heterogeneity, and limited heat transfer primarily govern the magnetocaloric response and low-field hysteresis in the target low-dimensional alloy.
Interfaces, grain boundaries, and surface disorder act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Constrained dimensionality in thin films and nanoribbons induces substantial structural disorder and strain.
Structural disorder and strain lead to a heterogeneous distribution of magnetic exchange interactions.
Localized domain-wall pinning suppresses coherent propagation of magnetic transitions.
Suppression of coherent magnetic-transition propagation reduces magnetocaloric efficiency.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases magnetic hysteresis.
Limited heat transfer compounds nonequilibrium behavior during fast magnetic-cooling cycles.
Moderate annealing below full crystallization partially relieves lattice strain.
Moderate annealing reduces interfacial and microstructural disorder.
Heat treatment can reduce the distribution of exchange energies and produce a more magnetically homogeneous high-entropy alloy.
Partial microstructural relaxation by annealing reduces domain-wall pinning.
Annealed samples will show a modest increase in magnetocaloric entropy change relative to as-deposited samples under identical low-field cycling conditions.
Annealed samples will show a reduction in hysteresis width relative to as-deposited samples under identical low-field cycling conditions.
As-deposited target films and nanoribbons have a depressed magnetocaloric response and pronounced hysteresis because of structural disorder and thermal limitations.
The proposed behavior applies near the magnetic phase transition under low-field, heat-transfer-limited cycling.

contradictions.description: The mechanism attributes heat-transfer-driven nonequilibrium to fast cycles, whereas the conditions and boundary emphasize low cycle frequencies and describe frequencies below a threshold for complete equilibration as heat-transfer limited. The relevant relation between frequency and equilibration is not consistently defined.
